steps.title: What is the NIE?
steps.body: The Foreigner ID Number is required for almost any official process in Spain: contracts, bank accounts, Social Security, self-employment. Requested at the Immigration Office or a Police station.

steps.title: Documents you'll need
steps.body: Valid passport (original and copy), completed EX-15 form, proof of payment of fee 790-012, and justification for the request (contract, bank account opening, etc.).

steps.title: Most common mistakes
steps.body: EX-15 form with details that don't match the passport, fee paid at the wrong bank, or missing original proof of the request's purpose.

steps.title: Booking your appointment (cita previa)
steps.body: Appointments are booked directly on the official portal, not through us: icp.administracionelectronica.gob.es/icpplus. Slots are scarce and get released periodically, often early morning — check back regularly. Never pay a third party for an appointment; that portal is the only official channel.

empadronamientoWizard.title: Procedure: Municipal registration
empadronamientoWizard.subtitle: Padrón — registering at your town hall

steps.title: What is the padrón?
steps.body: The padrón is the municipal register of residents. It's required to access public healthcare, enroll children in school, and as proof of address for many other procedures. Registration is done at your ayuntamiento (town hall).

steps.title: Documents you'll need
steps.body: A valid ID document (passport, NIE/TIE, or DNI) for every person being registered; proof of the address — a property deed or a rental contract in the applicant's name; and the padrón application form (hoja padronal), signed by every adult being registered.

steps.title: Most common mistakes
steps.body: A foreign ID document that doesn't show place or date of birth (some town halls then require a consular certificate); a rental contract that isn't in the applicant's name; and missing the owner's or tenant's signed authorization plus a copy of their ID when the applicant isn't on the title.

steps.title: Booking your appointment
steps.body: There's no single national booking system for the padrón — each ayuntamiento (town hall) manages its own. Search for your town hall's name plus "cita previa padrón" to find its booking page, or ask if walk-ins are accepted.

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: Registering as autónomo lets you legally invoice and work for yourself in Spain. It requires tax registration with the Agencia Tributaria and enrolling in Social Security's self-employed scheme (RETA).

steps.title: Documents you'll need
steps.body: Valid DNI or NIE (non-EU applicants need valid work authorization before registering); Modelo 036 tax registration with the Agencia Tributaria, stating your IAE/CNAE activity code and tax domicile; RETA registration via Import@ss (TA.0521) with the same activity code and start date, your estimated annual income, and a chosen mutua; and a bank account (IBAN) for the monthly quota.

steps.title: Most common mistakes
steps.body: Filing the old Modelo 037 — it's been discontinued, everything now goes through Modelo 036; an activity date on the RETA form that doesn't match the 036; underestimating income and ending up on the wrong contribution bracket; forgetting to choose a collaborating mutua; and non-EU nationals trying to register before their work authorization is actually granted.

steps.title: Where and when to file
steps.body: Both the 036 and the RETA registration are filed online, through the Agencia Tributaria's Sede Electrónica and Import@ss — no in-person appointment is required for the registration itself. File the RETA form on or before your first day of activity; it can be submitted up to 60 days in advance.

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: Before your first job in Spain, you need a Social Security number (Número de la Seguridad Social, NUSS, also called Número de Afiliación or NAF) to be registered for healthcare and benefits. It's requested at the nearest Social Security office (TGSS/INSS) using the TA.1 form.

steps.title: Documents you'll need
steps.body: A valid DNI, NIE, or passport; your contact details — a mobile phone number and email address; and your habitual address. All three are requested directly on the TA.1 form.

steps.title: Most common mistakes
steps.body: Requesting a new NUSS when the applicant already has one from a previous stay in Spain, which causes duplicates and delays; incomplete contact details on the TA.1; and an address on the form that doesn't match the one on the ID document.

steps.title: Booking your appointment
steps.body: Appointments are booked through the Social Security's official portal, sede.seg-social.gob.es, or by phone at 901 16 65 65. If you have a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN, some NUSS/NAF requests can be completed online without visiting an office at all.
